name: Substantiv
subtitle: Nouns: en/ett, definite forms and plural Groups 1–5

ruleCards.title: En or ett?
ruleCards.rule: Every noun is an en-word or an ett-word. About three in four are en-words. There is no reliable rule, so learn the article with the word.
ruleCards.watch: Words for people are almost always en-words: en lärare, en man, en kvinna. But: ett barn.

fun.sv: Det heter en stol men ett bord. Varför? Ingen vet. Inte ens stolen.
fun.en: It’s en stol (a chair) but ett bord (a table). Why? Nobody knows. Not even the chair.

ruleCards.title: En or ett? Clues from the ending
ruleCards.rule: Some endings tell you the gender. En-words: -ing, -het, -tion, -are, -ör, -ism, and most words in -a. Ett-words: -um, -eri, -ande, -ende, -em, -ment.
ruleCards.watch: Three body words in -a are ett-words: ett öga, ett öra, ett hjärta. People in -ande are en-words: en studerande.

fun.sv: Ett bageri säljer bröd, ett museum säljer biljetter och en programmerare säljer buggar som funktioner.
fun.en: A bakery sells bread, a museum sells tickets and a programmer sells bugs as features.
fun.note: Bageri (-eri) and museum (-um) are ett-words; programmerare (-are) is an en-word.

ruleCards.title: The definite form
ruleCards.rule: Swedish puts “the” at the end of the word. En-words add -en or -n, ett-words add -et or -t.
ruleCards.watch: Words ending in -el and -er often just add -n: nyckel → nyckeln, syster → systern.

fun.sv: Jag köpte en lampa på IKEA. Lampan är fin, men skruvarna är kvar i påsen.
fun.en: I bought a lamp at IKEA. The lamp is nice, but the screws are still in the bag.

ruleCards.title: Group 1: the -or house
ruleCards.rule: En-words that end in -a drop the a and add -or.
ruleCards.watch: A few words without -a also take -or: en ros → rosor.

fun.sv: En kaka, två kakor, tre kakor … nu finns det inga kakor kvar.
fun.en: One cake, two cakes, three cakes … now there are no cakes left.

ruleCards.title: Group 2: the -ar house
ruleCards.rule: Short concrete en-words, en-words with an e in one of the last two letters, and -ing words.
ruleCards.watch: The last e often disappears: fågel → fåglar, syster → systrar.

fun.sv: Det finns två sorters morgnar: tidiga morgnar och för tidiga morgnar.
fun.en: There are two kinds of mornings: early mornings and far too early mornings.
fun.note: En morgon, två morgnar: Group 2, and the o drops out.

ruleCards.title: Group 3: the -er and -r house
ruleCards.rule: Long en-words, words from other languages and words stressed on the last syllable add -er. En-words ending in a vowel other than a add only -r.
ruleCards.watch: Some short words change their vowel: bok → böcker, stad → städer, hand → händer, natt → nätter.

fun.sv: Hemma har vi fyra telefoner och tre datorer. Men ingen laddare.
fun.en: At home we have four phones and three computers. But no charger.

ruleCards.title: Group 3 exceptions
ruleCards.rule: These look like short Group 2 words, but they take -er. Learn them by heart.
ruleCards.watch: Vän doubles the n: vännen, vänner, vännerna.

fun.sv: Jag hade en katt. Nu har jag tre katter. Jag vet inte hur.
fun.en: I had one cat. Now I have three cats. I don’t know how.

ruleCards.title: Group 4: the -n house
ruleCards.rule: Ett-words that end in a vowel add -n.
ruleCards.watch: Irregular: ett öga → ögon, ett öra → öron.

fun.sv: Mormor har ett äppelträd. Nu har vi tvåhundra äpplen i köket.
fun.en: Grandma has an apple tree. Now we have two hundred apples in the kitchen.

ruleCards.title: Group 5: the no-ending house
ruleCards.rule: Ett-words that end in a consonant, and en-words for people ending in -are or -er, look the same in the plural.

fun.sv: Ett barn, två barn, tre barn. Ordet ändras inte, men ljudnivån gör det.
fun.en: One child, two children, three children. The word doesn’t change, but the noise level does.

ruleCards.title: Which plural group? A checklist
ruleCards.rule:
Go down the list and stop at the first yes.
1. Ett-word ending in a vowel: Group 4 (-n).
2. Other ett-word: Group 5 (no ending).
3. En-word ending in -a: Group 1 (-or).
4. En-word for a person in -are or -er: Group 5.
5. En-word in -e, -el, -en, -er, -ing or -dom: Group 2 (-ar).
6. En-word in -het or -tion, a borrowed word or one stressed at the end: Group 3 (-er).
7. Other vowel at the end: Group 3 (-r).
8. Short one-syllable en-word: usually Group 2 (-ar).
ruleCards.watch: Ett-words stressed at the end take -er: ett kafé → kaféer, ett bageri → bagerier. Ett-words in -um drop it: ett museum → museer. Short words like katt and sak are Group 3 exceptions.

fun.sv: En bugg, två buggar, tre buggar … och det är bara fredag eftermiddag.
fun.en: One bug, two bugs, three bugs … and it’s only Friday afternoon.
fun.note: Bugg is a short one-syllable en-word, so it goes to Group 2: buggar.

ruleCards.title: The definite plural
ruleCards.rule: Start from the plural. Groups 1–3 add -na, Group 4 adds -a, Group 5 ett-words add -en.
ruleCards.watch: En-words ending in -are drop the e: lärare → lärarna. Rum doubles the m: rummen.

fun.sv: Var är nycklarna? Var är glasögonen? Var är barnen? Okej, i bilen.
fun.en: Where are the keys? Where are the glasses? Where are the children? Okay, in the car.

ruleCards.title: Ingen, inget, inga
ruleCards.rule: Inte makes a verb negative. Ingen, inget, inga make a noun negative (“no, not any”). They follow the noun: ingen for en-words, inget for ett-words, inga for plurals.

fun.sv: Inget kaffe, ingen mjölk, inga bullar. Det är ingen morgon, det är en katastrof.
fun.en: No coffee, no milk, no buns. That’s not a morning, that’s a disaster.
fun.note: Inget for ett-words (kaffe), ingen for en-words (mjölk, morgon), inga for plurals (bullar).

ruleCards.title: Jag har ont i …
ruleCards.rule: To say something hurts, use ont i + the body part in the definite form.

fun.sv: Jag har ont i huvudet av alla en- och ett-ord.
fun.en: My head hurts from all the en-words and ett-words.
